citations.assessment: The opening paragraph names Yaakov of Kefar Ḥanin in its chain and also reports an alternate attribution.
The homily on peace in the heavens explicitly names Yaakov of Kefar Ḥanan.
The opening Eikhah exposition contains this Yaakov attribution within its chain of examples, using the phrase also cited separately from chapter 2.
Yaakov of Kefar Ḥanan identifies the friends as Michael and Gabriel.
The direct exposition attributes the torn mantle interpretation to Kefar Ḥanan, as in the opening chapter’s example.
The Midrash names Yaakov of Kefar Ḥanan and considers who was to father twelve tribes.
The exact parallel about dew expressly has Yaakov transmit in the name of Resh Lakish.
